title: Timed Paper 1 Section A practice paper and mark scheme, own questions
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y11 lesson 38 (Timed Paper 1 Section A practice paper and mark scheme, own questions (portal printable))
intro: Test. Answer every question in the spaces provided. Show your working: marks are given for method. The marks for each question are shown in brackets.

options: Heavy rain saturates soil, so run-off increases and the river floods.
questions.a: B) Heavy rain saturates soil, so run-off increases and the river floods.. It gives a reason and a consequence.

questions.q: A good case study point includes:
options: Place, detail and a link to the question
questions.a: B) Place, detail and a link to the question. Examiners reward specific, relevant detail.
B) Reduce primary jobs. Machines replace farm workers, who move to other sectors.

questions.q: Repeating a pedestrian count at three times of day improves:
questions.a: A) Reliability. More samples at different times give more reliable results.

options: Removing plant cover, exposing soil to erosion
questions.a: B) Removing plant cover, exposing soil to erosion. Bare soil is blown or washed away.

options: Plates collide and one may subduct
questions.a: B) Plates collide and one may subduct. Oceanic crust sinks beneath continental crust in subduction.

questions.q: Rewrite your two lowest-scoring mock answers in the portal response box using the mark scheme, then complete your repair list.
questions.a: Improved answers with developed points and place detail
questions.model: Teacher rewrites one anonymous Level 2 answer live.

questions.q: Answer: 'Explain two ways hard engineering can reduce coastal erosion.'
questions.a: e.g. sea walls reflect wave energy (2); rock armour absorbs wave energy (2)

questions.q: Write the conclusion for an 8-mark answer from your mock with clear criteria.
questions.a: Judgement linked to criteria and evidence

questions.q: Upgrade: 'Waves erode the cliff.' to a developed point.
questions.a: Destructive waves throw rocks at the cliff (abrasion) (1), wearing away the base and forming a wave-cut notch (1)
questions.model: Name the process: abrasion. Say how: rocks thrown at cliff. Say the result: notch forms.

questions.q: Rewrite your weakest Paper 2 extended answer with specific case study detail; then write your timing plan for Paper 2.
questions.model: Teacher rewrites one anonymous answer live.

questions.q: 'Explain why informal employment is common in megacities in developing countries.'
questions.a: Rapid migration and too few formal jobs (2); low skills and no barriers to entry, so people create their own work (2)

questions.q: Add a counter-argument to your extended answer.
Upgrade: 'Renewable energy is good.' using a named country.
questions.a: e.g. The UK's offshore wind farms (1) supply a growing share of electricity (1), cutting carbon emissions and imports (1)
questions.model: Name a place: UK. Give detail: offshore wind. Link: fewer emissions.

questions.q: Exam practice: (a) Calculate the difference between primary and tertiary employment in the example data. (1) (b) Explain two reasons for the decline of primary employment in developed countries. (4) (c) Assess the impact of informal employment in a named megacity. (8)
questions.a: (a) 35 percentage points (b) mechanisation; cheaper imports; growth of better-paid jobs elsewhere (c) balanced assessment with case detail and judgement

questions.q: Compare Malthus and Boserup in two sentences.
questions.a: Malthus: population outgrows food, causing crisis; Boserup: pressure drives invention and more food

questions.q: Using the example data, describe the employment structure.
questions.a: Primary is largest at 60% (1); secondary smallest at 15%, tertiary 25% (1)
questions.model: Largest sector with data. Smallest with data. Use figures.
